Eagles continue reshaping roster by reportedly releasing veteran wide receiver originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Hollywood Brown's brief and odd Eagles career is over after four games and five catches.

The Eagles are releasing Brown by mutual consent of the player and the team, Jordan Schultz of the Scultz Report posted on social media Thursday night.

The Eagles signed Brown to a one-year, $5 million contract in March with the expectation that he'd be a significant part of the Eagles' passing game following the departure of A.J. Brown. But even with Brown gone and DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks both hurt much of the season, Brown has been an afterthought.

He's only played in four of the Eagles' nine games, getting nine targets and catching five passes for 63 yards along with two rushing attempts for 12 yards. His longest catch was a 19-yarder from Tanner McKee in the loss to the Cowboys. He had a season-high 30 yards in that game.

Brown expressed frustration with his limited role in a recent conversation with NBC Sports Philadelphia:

"Of course, you want to be somewhere where you play, but at the ultimate end of the day, it's not my plan. So I might want to play, I might want to contribute, but if that's not the plan for me, I can't dwell on it too much or you'll be unhappy. And then you're taking that back home. I can't take that back home to the wife and kids. So I gotta try to stay as positive as I can."

Asked how that was going, he laughed and said, "Some days better than others."

He added: "We're all dealing with something and we're dealing with something as a team. So I don't wanna add that extra stress."

Brown said he expected to play more but was dealing with it because he didn't want to put personal issues ahead of team needs.

"I did (expect a bigger role), but I do understand stuff happens," he said. "I mean, you can't take anything personal in this business, so you kind of just got to go about your process and when that time happens, whatever happens, you've just got to be ready for it."

Brown, a 1st-round pick in 2019, had a 1,000-yard season for the Ravens in 2021 and over 700 yards in both 2020 and 2022. He was 49-for-587 with five touchdowns last year. In his career, he has 378 catches for 4,385 yards and 33 touchdowns.

The Eagles, 2-7, have lost seven straight game. Their offense is ranked 32nd in the NFL in yards per game, 30th in points per game and 29th in passing yards per game.

With Brown no longer on the roster, the Eagles have rookie 1st-round pick Makai Lemon, 2nd-year undrafted free agent Darius Cooper and Elijah Moore as healthy wide receivers. Smith and Wicks have both missed the last two games but could be back after the bye week.

Lemon is the Eagles' leading receiver with 37-for-312 and a touchdown and Smith (26-310-2), Wicks (19-284-1) and Cooper (13-200-4) are next.

The Eagles have two WRs on the practice squad – Erik Ezukanma and Xavier Gipson.

Because it's after the trade deadline, Brown is subject to the waiver claim process despite being a vested veteran with seven years of pension credit.

#2652. Observations after Sixers shake off slow start, Embiid injury scare to win

Observations after Sixers shake off slow start, Embiid injury scare to win originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers brushed off their blowout loss to the Celtics and got back in the win column Thursday night.

They overcame a first-quarter deficit as high as 17 points and earned a 123-112 home win over the Raptors. The Sixers moved to 10-3 and Toronto fell to 5-7.

Tyrese Maxey had 27 points and eight assists. Joel Embiid added 20 points.

Jaylen Brown tallied 18 points and six rebounds. VJ Edgecombe posted 15 points, eight rebounds and a season-high eight assists. Anfernee Simons scored 17 points and shot 5 for 6 from three-point range.

RJ Barrett recorded 31 points and 14 rebounds. Immanuel Quickley had 26 points and six assists.

The Sixers were without LeBron James (low back/sciatica management), Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear).

The team told reporters Thursday morning that Bona will be re-evaluated in approximately one week and that Barlow participated in shootaround. The 23-year-old forward also went through a pregame workout on the Xfinity Mobile Arena floor. There's no formal timetable for his return.

Toronto's sidelined players included Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes.

The Sixers will face the Pacers on Sunday afternoon in Philadelphia. Here are observations on their victory over the Raptors:

Dean Wade began the game in James' normal spot. The Sixers started slowly, missing their first foul field goals and opening 1 for 8 from three-point range.

He stayed down after setting a ball screen and having an apparent knee-to-knee collision with Ja'Kobe Walter. The Sixers called timeout with 8:30 left in the first quarter and Embiid grabbed at his right knee. He eventually rose with assistance from teammates and Sixers head athletic trainer Kevin Johnson, then limped back to the locker room. Jabari Walker entered.

At the 5:26 mark of the first quarter, Embiid checked back in to cheers from the home fans.

"I knew that he didn't twist it or anything," Maxey said. "I knew it was a knee-to-knee, so I wasn't too worried. He kept saying, 'I just got kneed.' That still hurts, though."

Embiid ended up logging 28 minutes, though he certainly wanted to play more.

"He was very, very motivated to play," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "It was hard to get him out for his scheduled rests tonight, which is a good problem sometimes."

While Embiid's return was a major positive development, the Sixers fell further behind. The Raptors' lead swelled to 32-16 with a Jamison Battle three-pointer and Nurse burned a timeout.

Simons sunk a buzzer-beating three to conclude the first quarter, cutting the Sixers' deficit to nine points.

"Those are big momentum plays that usually have some weight to them and carry you into the next moment," Nurse said.

The Sixers kept rolling against a shorthanded Toronto team playing on the second night of a back-to-back. Simons nailed a triple to kick off the scoring in the second quarter. Brown buried a mid-range jumper and Edgecombe jammed in a crowd-pleasing dunk to give the Sixers a 35-34 edge.

Brown and Edgecombe shined in the second quarter both as individuals and as a duo. The Sixers need Edgecombe to attack a bit more offensively when he shares the floor with Brown and bench players. It doesn't hurt for the second-year guard to have that clarity about his role in those units.

"He's one of our better playmakers," Maxey said of Edgecombe. "He's really good at getting downhill and creating for himself and others."

The Sixers' only three bench rotation players were Walker, Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope (11 points, five assists). In addition to Walker, Wade got center minutes behind Embiid.

Embiid picked up his third foul with 2:23 left in the second quarter and had to take a seat. The teams were tied at 60 apiece through two periods.

The game remained even for much of the third, but Maxey fueled an 11-0 Sixers run late in the quarter.

His speed and the Sixers' collective focus on pushing the pace whenever possible allowed the team to get regular points before Toronto could set its defense. Maxey zoomed in for a layup, then tossed the ball ahead to Brown for an easy bucket. Brown assisted a Simons three. Walker converted a fast-break lay-in and canned a three on the first possession of the fourth quarter. All of a sudden, the Sixers held a 101-87 lead.

Brown, Edgecombe and the bench gave the Sixers more good minutes early in the fourth quarter. They sealed the deal without any late drama. And the fans chanting for a Tacko Fall appearance got their wish with a final-minute entrance by the 7-foot-6 center.

#2650. Warning to NFL general managers: Howie Roseman is about to fleece you

Warning to NFL general managers: Howie Roseman is about to fleece you originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

A broken-down receiver, a washed-up guard and an underachieving defensive tackle walk into a bar. And Howie Roseman walks out with two 1st-round picks and three 2nd-round picks.

If I were an NFL general manager, I wouldn't even answer the phone when Howie calls. Because you're going to get fleeced.

And if there's one thing to feel good about during this miserable season to nowhere, it's the way Howie has stockpiled premium draft picks with a series of what sure seem like lopsided trades.

It all started in June when Roseman shipped disgruntled and divisive A.J. Brown to the Patriots for a 1st-round pick in 2027 and a 5th-round pick in 2027.

Brown was one of the best in the league not too long ago. He owns the two-best receiving seasons in Eagles history – 88-for-1,496 and 11 TDs in 2022 and 106-for-1,456-7 in 2023.

But it sure seems like his knees won't allow him to be that kind of player again. The A.J. Brown we saw hobbling around and dropping passes in his final game in an Eagles uniform, the playoff loss to the 49ers in January, seems to be closer to the player he is now than the Pro Bowler of a few years ago.

The Patriots got a WR whose balky knees have allowed him to play only three games so far this year, with just nine catches for 101 yards, three drops and a fumble.

Of 95 WRs who've been targetted at least 20 times so far this year, Brown's 15 percent drop percentage is highest. And his catch percentage is 89th. Maybe he gets healthy the second half of the season and reverts back to that three-time Pro Bowler. Or maybe this is just who A.J. Brown is right now. Either way the Eagles got a 1st-round pick for a guy who had no future in Philadelphia, didn't want to be here and may be a shot fighter at 29.

Then came the Cam Jurgens trade, and it's still hard to believe the Ravens donated the Eagles a 2nd-round pick for a guy who just hasn't been the same player as he was in 2024. Jurgens was a tremendous interior lineman before his career was derailed by injuries. Although he made a second straight Pro Bowl last year, he was only a shell of the player he was in 2023 and 2024. This year, he struggled both at center and guard before Howie someone finagled a 2nd-round pick out of the Ravens for him.

How has it gone in Baltimore for Jurgens? You always take Pro Football Focus grades with a grain of salt, but out of 89 interior linemen who've played at least 300 snaps his 43.9 combined grade with the Eagles and Ravens is 4th-worst.

In Jurgens' three games in Baltimore, the Ravens – with both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley hurt – have scored 33 points, gone 0-3, losing 35-13 to the Bengals, 36-10 to the Bills and 33-10 to the Jaguars after starting the season 4-1.

Then there's Jordan Davis. He was a good player here and at times a very good player. He probably should have made the Pro Bowl last year. But overall? As the 13th pick in the 2022 draft and the 10th-highest paid interior lineman in the league? He's underachieved, in particular this year. He was a key starter on two Super Bowl teams but he just never dominated the way you wanted him to, the way he's being paid to. And he played just 52 percent of the snaps in his nine games this year, which ranks 27th among starting interior linemen so far this year.

Great guy, natural leader, inspiring backstory, solid lineman. But hardly indispensable. Not when you also have Jalen Carter under contract and Moro Ojomo now in line for an offseason extension. The Eagles don't really have a third high-level rotational defensive tackle now – Ty Robinson, a 4th-round pick last year, will likely take over the role. But if you can get 1st- and 2nd-round draft picks for essentially a part-time player that's a no-brainer.

Add it up and Roseman got 1st-round picks in 2027 and 2028, 2nd-round picks in 2027, 2028 and 2029 and a couple 2027 5th-round picks to boot for a beat-up wide receiver, a fading interior lineman and a defensive tackle who hasn't lived up to expectations.

The way Roseman drafts, most of those picks are going to turn into important pieces as the Eagles build back toward respectability.

There hasn't been a whole lot to celebrate on the field this year, and everything points to more of the same over these last eight games.

But up on the second floor of the Jefferson Health Training Complex, Roseman is doing all he can to make sure it doesn't happen again.

#2649. Hurricanes leave Finland with sweep of Kraken

HELSINKI (AP) — Jordan Staal returned from injury, Andrei Svechnikov and Mark Jankowski each scored twice and the Carolina Hurricanes beat the Seattle Kraken 5-1 on Saturday to sweep the NHL's Global Series in Finland's capital.

The Hurricanes (16-3-2) followed on their dominant 4-1 victory on Thursday and extended their winning streak to four.

Carolina became the first NHL franchise to win each of its first four regular-season games played outside North America following a sweep of a 2010 series against the Minnesota Wild, also in Helsinki.

Jackson Blake also scored for the Hurricanes, Nikolaj Ehlers had three assists and Shayne Gostisbehere had two assists and Pyotr Kochetkov stopped 12 shots for his 12th win in 13 games.

Svechnikov scored on power plays with two identical goals from the right circle in the middle period, one-timing a precise snap shot to make it 3-0 and another for a 4-1 advantage. He has five goals in his four-game point streak and has 11 goals on the season.

His second goal with 9:55 left in the second period prompted the Kraken to pull Joey Daccord after he allowed four goals on 14 shots. Philipp Grubauer made 22 saves in relief.

CHICGO (AP) — Mark Scheifele had a goal and three assists, Kyle Connor scored a goal in regulation and had the deciding shootout goal, and Winnipeg rallied from a four-goal deficit to beat Chicago.

The Jets' sixth straight win was their second comeback from four goals down this season. They scored four times in 2:07 to beat Montreal 5-4 in overtime on Nov. 3.

Gabriel Vilardi's shot from the right slot tied the game 4-all with 1:13 left in regulation and goalie Nico Daws pulled for an extra attacker.

Scheifele also scored in the shootout. Daws stopped Roman Kantserov to lock up the victory.

BOSTON (AP) — Ryan Hartman and Danila Yurov scored two goals each, Jesper Wallstedt stopped 30 shots, and Minnesota beat Boston to extend their road winning streak to eight games.

Kirill Kaprizov extended his point streak to 11 games (six goals, 14 assists) with two assists for the West-leading Wild, who have earned at least a point in 11 straight games (9-0-2).

Quinn Hughes and Blake Coleman scored 67 seconds apart in the opening two minutes of the second period for Minnesota, which cruised to its NHL-best 10th road victory. Yurov scored both of his in the third period, the second an empty-netter.

David Pastrnak and Fraser Minten scored for Boston, which lost its second straight home game after winning seven in a row at TD Garden. Both losses came wearing their new mostly brown "varsity jerseys" with bright yellow numbers, trim and helmets that they debuted Thursday.

TORONTO (AP) — Connor McDavid extended his season-opening points streak to 21 games with an assist, Devon Levi made 19 saves for his first NHL shutout and Edmonton beat Toronto to hand the Maple Leafs their sixth straight home loss.

Defenseman Evan Bouchard scored his 12th goal of the season for Edmonton (15-3-3). The Oilers are 7-1-1 in their last nine games.

McDavid picked up an assist to give him 50 points (11 goals, 39 assists) and add to his NHL lead.

Oilers coach Mike Babcock faced his former team in Toronto for the first time since being fired in November 2019.

Anthony Stolarz stopped 22 shots for Toronto (8-12-2), which suffered its sixth consecutive regulation loss to complete a disastrous six-game stretch at Scotiabank Arena.

MONTREAL (AP) — Artturi Lehkonen had a goal and an assist and short-handed Colorado beat Montreal without injured stars Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar.

MacKinnon and Makar both sustained lower-body injuries Thursday night in a 4-3 overtime loss in Ottawa. Avalanche coach Jared Bednar said MacKinnon will be out at least a month, while Makar is expected to miss two weeks.

Fedor Svechkov, Brock Nelson and Nicolas Roy also scored for Colorado (12-6-3). Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 25 shots.

Nick Suzuki replied with a highlight-reel goal for Montreal (12-4-4), which had gone 12 consecutive games without losing in regulation (9-0-3).

Jakub Dobes made 22 saves in his first start in nine days.

TAMPA, Fla. (AP) — Daniil Tarasov stopped 31 shots for his second shutout of the season, Lucas Raymond had a goal and two points and Detroit beat Tampa Bay.

Michael Brandsegg-Nygard also scored to help the Red Wings snap a five-game losing streak.

Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 20 shots for Tampa Bay, which was shut out for the first time since December 8, 2025 at Toronto.

The Lightning lost for the first time at home this season, ending a franchise record eight-game home winning streak to start the season.

PITTSBURGH (AP) — Claude Giroux scored a goal and Ottawa beat Pittsburgh.

Giroux, the longtime Philadelphia Flyer, has 79 points in 74 career games against Pittsburgh. He's two points away from tying Sergei Fedorov (1,179) for 58th-place in NHL history.

Tim Stutzle scored his 11th goal of the season, and Michael Amadio and Thomas Chabot also had goals for the Senators, who have won five of their last seven games.

Linus Ullmark made 16 saves for his 200th NHL win.

Ullmark joined Martin Gerber as the only goalies in franchise history to start a season with nine wins in their first 10 appearances. Ullmark, who is 9-0-1 in 10 career games vs. Pittsburgh, has allowed two goals or fewer in 12 of his last 13 regular season starts.

Tommy Novak scored the lone goal for the Penguins, who have lost six of their last eight games.

WASHINGTON (AP) — Connor Hellebuyck recovered from a shaky start to make 43 saves, remaining unbeaten in net with New Jersey as the surging Devils defeated Washington.

Evan Rodrigues scored twice for the Devils, who earned their second win against Washington in three days. Jesper Boqvist, Connor Brown and Lenni Hameenaho each had a goal and two assists, and defenseman Luke Hughes added three assists.

Nico Hischier and Timo Meier also scored to help New Jersey improve to 11-2 since Oct. 20 with its seventh victory in eight games. Meier's power-play goal late in the second period gave the Devils their first lead, 4-3, and Hischier's short-handed goal made it 5-3 early in the third.

Rodrigues scored at 3:18 to make it 6-4 and added an empty-netter with 3:15 left.

COLUBUS, Ohio (AP) — Denver Barkey scored twice and Philadelphia rallied to beat Columbus, sending the Blue Jackets to their fourth consecutive loss and third straight at home.

Trevor Zegras and Matvei Michkov also scored, and Joseph Woll stopped 28 shots for Philadelphia, which won for the second time in its last six games and finished its five-game trip with points in four straight.

Dmitri Voronkov, Matthew Knies and Adam Fantilli scored for Columbus. Jet Greaves stopped 17 shots in his sixth straight loss.

Voronkov scored his first of the season at 3:19 of the first and Knies added a goal a minute later to give Columbus a 2-0 lead. Luca Del Bel Belluz, who replaced the injured Sean Monahan, notched his first assist of the season.

ST. LOUIS (AP) — Brady and Matthew Tkachuk participated in a pregame ceremony to honor their father, then led Florida to a win over St. Louis.

Brady Tkachuk scored the opening goal, and each brother had an assist in a dominant homecoming. Dmitry Kulikov, Anton Lundell and Sam Reinhart also scored, and Jacob Markstrom stopped 23 shots for Florida.

Dylan Holloway scored a power-play goal with 2:06 remaining as the Blues avoided being shut out in regulation for the second straight game. They defeated Utah 1-0 in a shootout Thursday night.

Brady Tkachuk scored 5:12 into the first period, beating goalie Joel Hofer on the glove side during an extended shift on the power play. His brother, Matthew, had the secondary assist after also drawing the high stick that gave Florida a 5-on-3 advantage following an early too-many-men penalty on St. Louis.

Keith Tkachuk, who concluded his 18-year career with the Blues, was honored in a pregame ceremony recognizing his induction last weekend into the Hockey Hall of Fame. His two sons, playing together in their hometown for the first time in the NHL, used two of Keith's old sticks during a ceremonial puck drop before the game. Then they showed why they're All-Stars in their own right.

DALLAS (AP) — Jake Oettinger made 22 saves to lead Dallas to a win over Buffalo, just two days after being pulled after allowing a season-high six goals.

It's Oettinger's fourth shutout this season and first since Oct. 17. Oettinger posted shutouts in three of Dallas' first six games — including a 4-0 win against Buffalo on Oct. 8 — but had allowed 14 goals in his past three starts, including six in an 8-3 loss to Winnipeg on Thursday.

Stars captain Jamie Benn snapped a scoreless game late in the second period with a goal for the 1,000th point of his 18-year career to give Dallas a 1-0 lead.

Wyatt Johnston took an assist from Mikko Rantanen and Roope Hintz and scored on a power play with 40 seconds remaining for the final score.

#2648. Embiid and James listed as questionable for Sixers vs. Raptors

Embiid and James listed as questionable for Sixers vs. Raptors originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers listed both Joel Embiid and LeBron James as questionable for their Thursday night game vs. the Raptors.

As has been the case on previous early-season injury reports, James' official listing was "low back/sciatica management" and Embiid's was "right foot plantar fascia injury management."

While Thursday's contest isn't part of a back-to-back, it's the sort of situation in which the Sixers have load management matters in mind for the 32-year-old Embiid and 41-year-old James. They'll host the Pacers on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET and then visit the Nets the following night.

James logged 29 minutes Tuesday in the 9-3 Sixers' loss to the Celtics and Embiid went 31. Embiid said postgame that he rolled his ankle late in the second quarter, but he was fine to play the second half.

With the Raptors facing Boston on Wednesday night, Toronto's complete injury report won't be available until Thursday afternoon. The Raptors announced Tuesday that superstar Kawhi Leonard will be sidelined for at least one more week because of his left knee injury.

Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear) will all remain out for the Sixers against the Raptors.

#2647. Drake London fined AGAIN for unnecessary roughness in Falcons’ loss to Bengals in Madrid

Drake London was fined for a second consecutive game, earning a $23,882 fine for unnecessary roughness/use of the helmet in the Falcons' frustrating loss to the Bengals in Madrid, Spain in Week 9.

The fine was levied for London's 21-yard catch with seconds left to play in the third quarter. London does lower his head as he makes contact with the Bengals defender on his way out of bounds, but does this really rise to the level of a $24k fine?

London's collected a few fines since being drafted by the Falcons in the first round of the 2022 NFL Draft. This season, he was fined $12,537 after Week 8 for unnecessary roughness against the Buccaneers. He was fined once for taunting in 2025, once for taunting in 2024, and he was fined in his rookie season for an "excessive face mask."

No Bengals were fined for their play against the Falcons in Madrid. Cincinnati won the game, 34-17.

The NFL splits the money it collects for player accountability equally between the NFLPA's support of retired players, the NFL Foundation, and other nonprofits supporting youth sports, community health and fitness initiatives, and player health and safety at every level of sports.

#2646. Georgia marks return to No. 1 by routing Missouri behind Frazier and Stockton

ATHENS, Ga. (AP) — Nate Frazier ran for three touchdowns, Gunner Stockton accounted for a pair of scores and Georgia marked its return to No. 1 by racing to a 31-point lead in the first half on the way to a victory over Missouri.

The Bulldogs (9-1, 6-1 Southeastern Conference, No. 1 CFP) scored on their first five possessions in another dominant win, ensuring this trip to the top of the rankings will last more than one week.

A month ago, Georgia moved up to No. 1 for the first time this season — and promptly took a shocking home loss to unranked Auburn.

No such issues this time with another set of Tigers (6-4, 3-4, No. 22 CFP).

Frazier scored on three short runs and finished with 72 yards on 14 carries. Stockton was 18 of 24 for 252 yards and a TD, with a rushing score for good measure. The Georgia defense dominated until garbage time, holding the Tigers to 286 total yards.

The tone was set on the very first play from scrimmage. Austin Simmons was picked off by Georgia's Raylen Wilson, who returned his first career interception 30 yards to the Missouri 7. Two snaps later, Frazier ran it in from the 4 to give the Bulldogs the lead just 1:01 into the game.

SOUTH BEND, Ind. (AP) — CJ Carr passed for 217 yards and two touchdowns, and Notre Dame showed no letdown after knocking off Miami last week, beating Boston College.

Notre Dame beat then-No. 1 Miami 31-24 last Saturday. The Fighting Irish (9-1) returned Saturday and rolled to a 31-0 halftime lead.

Carr completed 20-of-28 passes, including a 26-yard TD pass to Micah Gilbert and a 13-yard scoring strike to Jordan Faison.

Freshman running back Jonaz Walton gained 141 yards on 15 carries and scored on a 1-yard run. Nolan James Jr. added 73 yards rushing and a 10-yard TD.

Jaylen Sneed scored 1-yard scoop-and-score touchdown off a fumble forced by Boubacar Traore. The Fighting Irish limited Boston College to 136 yards of total offense.

MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. (AP) — Darian Mensah passed for 382 yards and a touchdown against his former school, Javian Mallory scored three times and Miami moved closer to wrapping up a trip to the Atlantic Coast Conference title game by beating Duke.

Mark Fletcher Jr. also rushed for a score for Miami (9-1, 7-0 ACC, No. 7 CFP), which tied a school mark with its 11th consecutive ACC victory. Cooper Barkate — like Mensah, a former Duke star — had his first 100-yard game for Miami, catching eight passes for 134 yards.

Mensah, who transferred to Miami after leading Duke to last season's ACC title, completed 30 of 41 passes for Miami and went over the 3,000-yard mark for the season.

Nate Sheppard accounted for 240 yards — 131 rushing, 93 receiving and 16 passing — plus rushed for two scores and caught a conversion pass for Duke (7-3, 5-3). Sheppard had a pair of 47-yard runs in the game, along with 12 catches.

Walker Eget completed 26 of 42 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown for the Blue Devils, but was intercepted by Miami's Xavier Lucas with 6:54 left. Mallory's 39-yard touchdown run on the ensuing possession sealed the win for Miami.

Miami's win, combined with Wake Forest's win over SMU, put the Hurricanes on the cusp of clinching a spot in the ACC title game. The Hurricanes would wrap up a berth in the Dec. 5 contest if North Carolina beats Louisville later Saturday night; otherwise, Miami needs only one win in its final two games to clinch.

BLOOMINGTON, Ind. (AP) — Grant Wilson threw two touchdown passes in his first start for Indiana, Khobie Martin scored on a 1-yard run and the Hoosiers had two late interceptions to preserve a crucial victory over USC.

The victory helps Indiana (9-1, 6-1 Big Ten, No. 9 CFP) solidify its postseason resume after falling five spots in this week's playoff rankings. Indiana has won three straight since losing to then-No. 2 Ohio State, and this time they did it with Wilson filling in for Josh Hoover. Coach Curt Cignetti said Hoover was healthy but he went with Wilson anyway.

Wilson had an up-and-down day, finishing 17 of 27 for 305 yards and one interception. Lee Beebe Jr. had 16 carries for 71 yards while Martin had 10 carries for 70 yards and the tiebreaking score with 2:39 left in the third quarter. Charlie Becker added a 42-yard TD catch with 3:30 left, making 27-13.

The Trojans (7-3, 4-3, No. 18) needed a victory to keep their playoff — and Big Ten title hopes alive, but only scored one TD in five red-zone trips. Jayden Maiava was 26 of 42 for 311 yards and one TD but was picked off three times — twice in the fourth quarter, one of those inside the Hoosiers' 5. Trent Mosley caught nine passes for 130 yards.

NASHVILLE, Tenn. (AP) — Keelon Russell threw for 217 yards and three touchdowns, and Alabama beat Vanderbilt Saturday in an ugly game that did little to help the Crimson Tide's stock for the College Football Playoff.

Alabama (8-2, 6-2 SEC) came in third in the CFP rankings but struggled for the first half against a team that came in having recently snapped a five-game skid. The Crimson Tide led only 7-3 at halftime thanks to Russell's 9-yard TD pass to Marshall Pritchett.

The Crimson Tide had five sacks and held Vanderbilt (4-6, 1-6) to a season-low 235 yards of total offense. The Commodores also turned it over on downs on three of their final four drives, twice inside the Alabama 15, and also missed a field goal late.

Vanderbilt forced three turnovers: a turnover on downs, Dontae Carter intercepted a pass, and Miles Capers forced a fumble by Russell recovered by Talan Carter. The Commodores held Alabama to 92 yards rushing.

The Crimson Tide had zero rushing yards after Russell slipped to the turf for a big loss and a turnover on downs early in the second quarter. Russell, who started after hurting an ankle in last week's win at LSU, also had a pass batted into the air by Carter for his first career interception.

BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — Arch Manning — like his grandfather and uncle before him — has a Death Valley comeback story to tell.

Manning found Raleek Brown for a 4-yard touchdown pass along the left sideline with 3 seconds left, and Texas escaped Tiger Stadium with a victory over LSU.

The dramatic win in the state where Manning was raised — and in a stadium where he attended games as a kid — kept Texas (8-2, 5-2 SEC) firmly in contention for a College Football Playoff spot while virtually eliminating LSU (6-4, 3-4).

Manning, who also rushed for an early score, was an unspectacular 19-of-35 passing for 174 yards and one touchdown with three interceptions. But he looked made for the moment when Texas began its final drive on its own 42, down 21-16, with 2:19 left.

He converted three third downs — one with a 5-yard pass and two with his legs — to set up his decisive scoring strike into the end zone near where his celebrating parents, Cooper and Ellen, were sitting.

COLLEGE STATION, Texas (AP) — DaSaahn Brame had a touchdown catch and Cooper Ranvier made a career-high five field goals to lead Tennessee to a win over Texas A&M.

DeSean Bishop added 97 yards rushing to help the Volunteers, who ranked eighth in this week's College Football Playoff rankings, to their fifth win in six games.

The Aggies led 7-6 at halftime and neither team could get anything going offensively in the third quarter as they combined for five punts.

Tennessee (8-2, 5-2 SEC) finally got going and took a 9-7 lead on a 32-yard field goal by Ranvier late in the third.

The Aggies (4-6, 1-6) looked to have forced a punt on Tennessee's next drive. But Marco Jones was called for roughing the passer to give the Volunteers a first down.

Tennessee took advantage of the error when Faizon Brandon threw a 5-yard touchdown pass to Brame that made it 16-7 with less than 10 minutes to go.

The Aggies went for it on fourth-and-1 from their 34 on their next possession, but Reed's pass was incomplete to give Tennessee great field position.

They padded the lead with a 44-yard field goal that left them up 19-7 with about six minutes left.

Ranvier added a 27-yard field goal with less than three minutes to go to make it 22-7.

DALLAS (AP) — Gio Lopez ran for two touchdowns and threw for a score, and Wake Forest extended its winning streak to seven games while strengthening a case for a playoff spot with a blowout of SMU.

The Demon Deacons (9-1, 6-1 ACC) led 42-0 at halftime while handing the Mustangs (7-3, 5-3) their first Atlantic Coast Conference loss at home in the Ford Stadium finale of their third ACC season. SMU entered 12-0 at home in league games.

Wake Forest, which was 13th in this week's rankings for the 12-team College Football Playoff, opened the scoring with Ty Clark's 27-yard touchdown on third-and-18, the first of four first-half TDs on third down. Another 1-yard score was set up by Jamar Searcy's 38-yard run on fourth-and-1.

Kevin Jennings threw for 209 yards with a touchdown and an interception while falling to 16-2 at home in his final Ford Stadium start. He had just 40 yards passing late in the first half when the deficit was 42-0.

Flickering CFP hopes were all but snuffed out for the Mustangs, who began the year hoping for a second playoff trip in three ACC seasons with Jennings while making a Heisman Trophy push for their hometown quarterback.

COLUMBUS, Ohio (AP) — Luke Fahey passed for 201 yards and three touchdowns, Jeremiah Smith had 11 receptions for 117 yards and a score, and Ohio State beat Northwestern.

Bo Jackson had 114 yards rushing and a touchdown as the Buckeyes (7-3, 5-2 Big Ten) bounced back after losing two straight regular-season games for the first time since 2011.

Northwestern quarterback Nicco Marchiol had 225 yards passing and accounted for both Wildcats touchdowns, but it wasn't enough as they lost their third straight game. Jackson Kleather kicked two field goals.

Luke Dehnicke made a nice 18-yard TD grab in the end zone on the last play of the game.

Marchiol's 2-yard scramble around right end got Northwestern (6-4, 3-4) within 14-13 with 10:01 remaining in the third quarter before Ohio State regained control. The Buckeyes went 83 yards in 13 plays on the ensuing drive, which was capped by Devin McCuin's 8--yard TD catch. On fourth-and-1, Fahey rolled left and McCuin caught it at the 1 before he powered past Northwestern defensive back Ore Adeyi to reach the end zone.

Ohio State's maligned special teams then came up with a big play when Dalton Riggs recovered a muffed punt by Drew Wagner at the Northwestern 10. Three plays later, Smith had his 15th touchdown of the season on a 2-yard catch to put the Buckeyes up by two scores.

WACO, Texas (AP) — Bear Bachmeier ran for three touchdowns and threw for another score to lead BYU to a victory over Baylor.

Bachmeier totaled 158 yards of offense and powered a rushing attack that piled up 189 yards. LJ Martin added 49 yards on six carries for the Cougars (8-2, 5-2 Big 12, No. 10 CFP) but did not play in the second half after suffering an apparent ankle injury just before halftime.

DJ Lagway threw for 159 yards and a touchdown to lead the Bears. Baylor (6-4, 4-3) had a two-game winning streak snapped after struggling to do anything on offense before the fourth quarter.

BYU ran all over Baylor's defense in the first half. The Cougars scored touchdowns on their first three drives while racking up 150 yards on the ground and averaging 5 yards per carry.

LEXINGTON, Ky. (AP) — Florida quarterback Aaron Philo had 221 all-purpose yards and a touchdown to rally the Gators past Kentucky.

Philo, back in the starting lineup after being benched against Georgia on Oct. 31, threw for 119 yards and ran for 102, including the go-ahead score on a 2-yard run with 9:08 left in the game. Jaden Baugh also scored his SEC-leading 15th touchdown for Florida (6-4, 4-4), now bowl eligible.

Kentucky (7-3, 5-3) dropped its second straight game as the offense struggled to move the ball after an opening 86-yard touchdown drive. The Wildcats crossed midfield three times but the Gator defense, coached by former Kentucky defensive coordinator Brad White, turned them back.

Kentucky quarterback Kenney Minchey threw for 181 yards and a touchdown, but the Wildcat rushing game was non-existent with just 61 yards.

IOWA CITY, Iowa ( AP) — Hank Brown threw for a touchdown and ran for another, LJ Phillips rushed for 123 yards and Iowa beat Purdue.

The Hawkeyes (8-2, 5-2 Big Ten) won their third consecutive game behind an offense that had 434 yards and a defense that held the Boilermakers (3-7, 2-5) to their lowest points total of the season.

Brown had a 1-yard touchdown run to open the scoring for Iowa, then threw a short pass that Braeden Jackson turned into a 44-yard touchdown late in the first half that gave the Hawkeyes a 21-7 halftime lead.

Phillips had his second consecutive 100-yard rushing game. He had 128 yards in Iowa's 24-10 win over Northwestern last Saturday.

BOISE, Idaho (AP) — Rasean Jones caught 11 passes for 230 yards and three touchdowns to help Boise State outlast Oregon State and wrap up the host spot in the Pac-12 championship game Dec. 4.

Maddux Madsen, who missed the previous game with an injury, was 23 of 32 for a career-best 371 yards and four touchdowns to help the Broncos (9-1, 6-0 Pac-12, No. 24 CFP) win their ninth straight game.

Jones had his third consecutive 100-yard game, gaining a career-best 134 yards in the first half alone. He had the fifth-best game receiving total in Boise State history.

The matchup featured two of the top freshmen pass-catchers in the nation, Jones and the Beavers' Jesse Legree. Entering the game as the leader in yards receiving and receiving touchdowns in the Football Bowl Subdivision, Legree had 12 catches for 140 yards and a touchdown for the Beavers (5-5, 3-3) .

Oregon State's Maalik Murphy, stepping in for injured starter Braden Atkinson, completed 31 of 39 passes for 396 yards, three touchdowns and an interception.

EUGENE, Ore. (AP) — Dylan Raiola threw for 341 yards and four touchdowns, and Oregon kept its slim chances for a spot in the College Football Playoff alive with a 31-7 victory over struggling Michigan on Saturday.

Jeremiah McClellan caught four passes for 105 yards and a score for the Ducks (7-3, 5-2 Big Ten), who are No. 16 in the CFP rankings. Oregon has won three straight games.

Michigan (5-5, 2-5) is still seeking a sixth win to become bowl-eligible in the Wolverines' first season under coach Kyle Whittingham. Michigan was coming off a 15-6 loss at home to rival Michigan State, and a day later the team fired first-year offensive coordinator Jason Beck.

Whittingham was familiar with the Ducks and Autzen Stadium because of his long tenure at Utah in the Pac-12 before the conference collapsed in the summer of 2023.

Whittingham shook things up against Oregon by using both Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood at quarterback after Carr had been the starter for the past three games. But the two QBs combined for just 71 yards passing against the Ducks.

FAYETTEVILLE, Ark. (AP) — KJ Jackson threw for 188 yards and two touchdowns and Arkansas took advantage of four turnovers by South Carolina to beat the Gamecocks.

It was the Razorbacks' first Southeastern Conference victory at home since Nov. 5, 2024 against Tennessee, which was also the last time Arkansas (4-6, 2-5) beat a ranked opponent. South Carolina's loss snapped a four-game winning streak.

Both of Jackson's touchdown passes came in the second quarter as Arkansas built a 17-0 halftime lead. He found Chris Marshall for a 23-yard score for the team's first touchdown and then connected with Antonio Jordan for a 28-yard score on the next drive.

South Carolina's offense struggled without starting quarterback LaNorris Sellers, who did not play after injuring his ankle in the team's win over Texas A&M Nov. 7. Cutter Woods played the entire game, going 24 of 43 passing for 271 yards with three interceptions.

COLUMBUS, Ohio (AP) — Luke Fahey passed for 201 yards and three touchdowns, Jeremiah Smith had 11 receptions for 117 yards and a score, and Ohio State beat Northwestern.

Bo Jackson had 114 yards rushing and a touchdown as the Buckeyes (7-3, 5-2 Big Ten) bounced back after losing two straight regular-season games for the first time since 2011.

Northwestern quarterback Nicco Marchiol had 225 yards passing and accounted for both Wildcats touchdowns, but it wasn't enough as they lost their third straight game. Jackson Kleather kicked two field goals.

Luke Dehnicke made a nice 18-yard TD grab in the end zone on the last play of the game.

ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. (AP) — Jackson Arnold threw a long fourth-quarter touchdown pass and ran for another score and UNLV beat New Mexico, spoiling the Lobos' first home game in The Associated Press poll.

Arnold threw for 201 yards and two touchdowns and rushed for 98 yards to help UNLV (6-4, 4-2 Mountain West) beat the Lobos (8-2, 5-1) on the road for the fifth straight time.

The Rebels fell behind 14-0 as New Mexico relied on its power rushing game and stout defense.

Scottre Humphrey went over from 3 yards in the first quarter for the Lobos, and Cade Keith caught a 9-yard touchdown pass from Toa Fa'avae in the second quarter, but New Mexico could not quite generate enough offense the rest of the way.

#2645. "I feel at home”: A day in the life of RB Leipzig midfielder El Aynaoui

Moroccan international Neil El Aynaoui has started every Bundesliga and Champions League game since completing his switch from AS Roma to RB Leipzig on the deadline day on an initial loan deal. The 25-year-old midfielder shared his routines in Leipzig in the latest episode of the “Day in Life” series produced by the club.

The tour started with El Aynoaui enjoying his breakfast at home alongside his father Younes, a former top-20 ATP tennis player. He then drove his father's classic car to get to Leipzig's training center in Cottaweg, discussing his adaptation to life in Leipzig on his way to joining his teammates for a training session and recovery work.

“I used to live in the North of France. The life here (in Leipzig) is pretty the same,” the former RC Lens central midfielder said. “The team makes me feel comfortable. Every person who works at the club is honestly top. The facilities and the stadium are top.”

Leipzig coach Martin Demichelis is also new to the club, and El Aynaoui believes the Argentine has helped him to quickly adapt to the surroundings.

“The coach makes me feel at home. I also talked with him before arriving here. My teammates also make me feel at home. It's easier for me," he said.

The 25-time Moroccan international didn't want to pick a specific name when he was asked which player he has a special friendship with. “I'm gonna say the French guys. The guys who speak French."

“I actually started playing in Spain,” El Aynaoui said, revisiting his early years as a footballer.

“After I went to France, I spent most of my career at Nancy. Then I left for a bigger club in France, Lens, to play in the Champions League and first division.”

El Aynaoui made his first team debut in Ligue 2 for his hometown club before captaining them at the young age in the third tier the following season. Within a matter of months, he replaced Championnat National (the current Ligue 3) with Champions League football after a move to RC Lens.

“I played two years at Lens. It was fantastic and the club is amazing. And we're gonna face them in the Champions League this season. I'm happy to play against them,” El Aynaoui added regarding his second professional club, who are currently in a difficult state after their 9-1 home defeat to Como in the same competition already forced them to a second managerial shake-up.

“Last year, I played in Italy with Roma. And I'm now here,” El Aynaoui said at the end of going over his past clubs before speaking highly of the German mentality. “In France, we say you (Germans) are disciplined. The work rate is very important here, and I like it.”

While he spoke to RB Leipzig's media team on his way to training this time, El Aynaoui revealed that his morning routine usually involves catching up with family over the phone, emphasising the importance of staying in touch with those close to him.

After an intense training session on a sunny day, El Aynaoui completed recovery sessions in the treatment room and Leipzig's gym.

On this specific day, he took part in a tennis challenge against 2020 US Open winner Dominic Thiem after leaving the training center. His father, Younes El Aynaoui, and Maxime Estève, who also joined RB Leipzig in the summer, accompanied the duo on the tennis court.

Before preparing to end the day by watching a movie, El Aynaoui dined with his teammate Estève. “I like thrillers. My favorite movie is Shutter Island. I like a movie with a plot twist.” he said about his affection for American films.

Unlike last month, El Aynaoui will spend the international break in Leipzig as he withdrew from Morocco's squad to undergo treatment for a minor calf problem. The Atlas Lions will play against Niger in Casablanca and Rabat in their next two games in the AFCON 2027 qualifiers.

#2644. ‘Hard to win': Simons, Walker carry Portland lessons into Sixers roles

'Hard to win': Simons, Walker carry Portland lessons into Sixers roles originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Anfernee Simons and Jabari Walker shared the floor for 128 games in Portland. The Trail Blazers won 43 of them.

They sat beside one another in the Sixers' interview room Thursday night after a victory and discussed what the other 85 taught them.

"Whether you've got a big role or a small role, it's hard to win in the NBA," Simons said. "We've seen it firsthand."

Their roles were considerably different then.

Simons was an established starter entrusted with creating and scoring. Walker, a 2022 second-round pick, was trying to establish himself in a rotation. During their three overlapping seasons, Portland went 33-49, 21-61 and 36-46. The Blazers missed the playoffs each year.

Both are now reserves on a Sixers team constructed to contend. In nine games they've both appeared in this season, Philadelphia is 7-2.

They provided 26 points, 11 rebounds and six three-pointers in the Sixers' 123-112 win over the Raptors at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Simons scored 17 points and shot 5 for 6 from three-point range. Walker recorded nine points and eight rebounds, including four on the offensive glass.

The Sixers outscored Toronto by 24 points during Simons' 23 minutes. Neither former Blazer committed a turnover.

Their production helped Philadelphia overcome a 17-point first-quarter deficit and improve to 10-3 without LeBron James.

"You learn once you come off the bench to kind of read the game before you get in there," Simons said. "Obviously, we started off kind of slow. You just want to go in, bring some energy, get some stops, get out and run. I think everybody who got off the bench brought energy."

Simons supplied an immediate lift with a deep three-pointer at the first-quarter buzzer. His shot ended an 8-0 Sixers run and trimmed Toronto's lead to nine.

He remained involved during an 11-0 burst late in the third quarter, knocking down a three and setting up Walker for a basket. Walker then made a three early in the fourth before Simons scored on the Sixers' next possession.

When Toronto pulled within six with less than five minutes remaining, Simons answered with his fifth three-pointer.

Making those shots is the most obvious way Simons can help a roster already featuring James, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown. He said the Sixers have not made him feel as though every opportunity must go in.

"They encourage us to keep shooting the ball," Simons said. "Knowing that a team has that much confidence in us to keep shooting makes the game that much easier. Whether you miss or make, as long as we get the right shots in the right moments, I think everybody can live with the misses and makes."

Simons spent seven seasons in Portland before playing last year with Boston and Chicago. His move to Philadelphia reunited him with Walker and Rayan Rupert, another former Blazer who joined the Sixers on a two-way contract during the offseason.

Knowing familiar faces awaited him helped Simons enter another new locker room.

"It made the transition seamless," he said. "Just being able to have some comfortability with guys that I played with for multiple years. It's been fun, kind of feeling like a little bit of old times. Me, Bari and Rups have been through a lot."

Walker's path to Philadelphia began a year earlier and required an additional step.

After playing 188 games over three seasons with Portland, Walker signed a two-way contract with the Sixers in July 2025. He earned a standard contract in February and has since pushed his way into the backup-center conversation despite standing 6-foot-7.

Walker believes some of the work he did on losing teams was easily missed.

"When I first got to the league, I was part of a rebuilding process," he said. "I just felt like some of the little things I did didn't always get noticed when you're losing. I told myself, if I ever got to be part of a winning organization, then I'd go out and expand my abilities."

Rebounding has made Walker difficult for Nick Nurse to overlook.

Walker credited his timing and strong hands to lessons passed down by his father, former NBA center Samaki Walker. Those instincts have become especially useful while the Sixers piece together their frontcourt behind Embiid.

"Rebounding is a skill I kind of honed in on," Walker said. "My dad was a good rebounder. He was known for his rebounding and his timing. I think it's just a gift that he transferred to me."

Walker has made it clear that he expected to earn a role this season.

"I don't know if I was delusional, but I always felt like I was going to play and I was going to be a part," he said. "I read something where they said it's a surprise, but if you were around me this summer, it wouldn't be a surprise. This is expected, and I just want to continue to get better."

The freedom Simons once had in Portland is no longer necessary. Walker does not need a high volume of touches, either. Both understand that playing beside the Sixers' stars requires shooting when open, moving the ball and handling the less glamorous work.

"You've got to find ways to impact the game multiple ways, even if you're not scoring," Simons said. "Whether it's cutting, making the right read and pass to Joel, being the right swing pass to VJ, boxing out on defense or just being in the right position."

Their opportunities will fluctuate. Simons may take nine shots one night and only a few the next. Walker's minutes will depend on matchups and the health of Philadelphia's frontcourt.

Winning has changed what they are being asked to do. Their three years together in Portland taught them why the adjustment is worthwhile.

"You feel appreciative of the times where you go into a situation where your role might be a little bit less, but you're winning," Simons said. "That's something you can't take for granted."

#2643. What placing TreVeyon Henderson on IR, activating Greg Van Roten and Reggie Gilliam means for the Patriots

At around 10 p.m. local time in Germany on Saturday, the New England Patriots announced that they have made some changes to their roster. Running back TreVeyon Henderson was headed to injured reserve due to the illness that has kept him out since late October, while fullback Reggie Gilliam and offensive lineman Greg Van Roten were both activated from IR.

With the Patriots having entered the weekend at 52 players on their roster, Saturday's transactions meant that they now have a full complement of players available again. What else do the moves mean, though? Let's find out.

TreVeyon Henderson taking to social media last Friday already was an ominous sign. In a statement addressing the illness that had kept him out for more than a week at that point, he mentioned that "my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions" were affected by the "unexpected and unusual medical emergency" he had been dealing with.

While there might still have been hope at that point that he would be able to return in a relatively short period of time, Saturday's move means that that will not be the case.

Henderson will be out for at least the next four games, starting with the upcoming contest against the Detroit Lions. Other games he is now slated to miss include matchups with the Chargers, Bills and Vikings. He is eligible to return to practice and off injured reserve ahead of the Patriots' Week 15 game in Kansas City, even though an obvious question mark hangs over that comeback given the most recent information we have available — information, head coach Mike Vrabel also did not add to this week.

"I talk to TreVeyon every day and just like everybody else that's not available, he's working hard to get back," he said on Thursday at the FC Bayern Munich training facility. "When that is I don't know. I don't have a timetable, but I love my interactions with him. I love talking with him and seeing how he's doing."

From a football perspective, Henderson going to IR officially removes the No. 2 running back from the Patriots' active roster. This leaves the group looking as follows:

53-man roster (3): Rhamondre Stevenson (38), Corey Kiner (9 | KR), Lan Larison (34)

Practice squad (1): Terrell Jennings (26)

IR (2): Myles Montgomery (39 | season-ending), TreVeyon Henderson (32)

Rhamondre Stevenson is the clear top option, something that would not change with Henderson available. He is the Patriots' most reliable back in all aspects of playing the position, and by far their best pass protector at the position. Still, Henderson as a rotational second option would bring a more dynamic element to the table than the likes of Corey Kiner and Lan Larison. That element is now missing, even though Kiner in particular has had some promising moments as of late and given Stevenson's unclear outlook — he is questionable with a knee injury — might see increased reps versus Detroit.

In addition to the roster perspective, Henderson going to IR also adds to the numbers crunch regarding the return spots. As a reminder, the Patriots had eight of those available at the start of the year but already used five on the likes of wide receivers A.J. Brown and Mack Hollins, offensive tackle Marcus Bryant and the aforementioned Reggie Gilliam and Greg Van Roten.

Two of the remaining three are expected to go to a pair of starters, wide receiver Romeo Doubs and left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker. This, in turn, would potentially leave one such spot open for Henderson. Of course, if they were to qualify for the postseason, the Patriots would get two extra IR-return opportunities.

Gilliam went to injured reserve after the Patriots' Week 4 win over the Bills. He had been dealing with a knee injury entering that contest, and additionally suffered an ankle ailment in that particular game.

New England did not have a traditional fullback on the 53-man roster or practice squad at that point, and never added one either since initially losing Gilliam. This also meant that the fullback packages that were used earlier in the season were not further expanded upon, which in turn might have also played its part in the Patriots struggling to consistently move the football on the ground.

Gilliam returning will not instantly fix those issues, but he should be an immediate upgrade over the player the team primarily used to replace him, since-released rookie tight end Tanner Arkin. At the very least, the Patriots can begin incorporating those packages on a more regular and purposeful basis again.

In addition to the offensive element, Gilliam's return also might have a positive impact on the Patriots' special teams operation. His leadership has been praised repeatedly by coordinator Jeremy Springer, while he also might resume the three-unit role he played prior to his stint on IR: he was used on kickoff coverage, kickoff return and punt coverage, playing 41% of kicking game snaps over the first four weeks of the season.

The kickoff coverage element in particular will be worth watching after the Patriots have had multiple breakdowns over the last few weeks. Adding as experienced a special teamer as Gilliam to the mix might help fix those issues.

We know that the Patriots offensive line is going to look different compared to the one that started last Sunday's game against the Packers. The only question is how different.

Obviously, three spots are set in stone as they very much have been for the entire season: Will Campbell and Morgan Moses will be the starting tackles, with Jared Wilson at center. The guard positions, meanwhile, remain a revolving door.

Before looking into the options for Sunday and further into the future, let's set the scene by looking at which interior O-linemen are, and are not, available right now:

53-man roster (5): Ben Brown (77 | LG), Jared Wilson (55 | C), Matt Pryor (65 | RG), Greg Van Roten (70), Walter Rouse (72)

Practice squad (2): Xavier Newman-Johnson (64), Andrew Rupcich (67)

IR (2): Mike Onwenu (71), Alijah Vera-Tucker (75)

Ben Brown, who started last week at left guard, will not be available on Sunday against the Lions because of the knee injury he suffered in Week 9. This creates an opening Van Roten might be asked to fill, despite the fact that he played just one non-preseason snap at the position over the last seven years; the last time he played left guard extensively, Tom Brady was still the quarterback in New England.

The problem is that the alternatives are not overly attractive either, especially looking at the Lions game. Matt Pryor has limited LG experience as well, while moving him would introduce change at two spots within a unit whose success depends largely on the chemistry between its individual members. Walter Rouse, meanwhile, is questionable to play in the game after showing concussion symptoms coming out of last week's game versus the Packers.

And so, Van Roten might still be the best option after all. Long-term, however, the goal is to bring Alijah Vera-Tucker back into the mix; who will then start at right guard between Pryor, Van Roten or Brown is a question for another time.

#2642. Christian Pulisic sends message with double vs. Haiti in USMNT return

MIAMI — Next week, the U.S. men's national team will no longer be Mauricio Pochettino's team.

The manager is headed to take over Manchester United, returning to the Premier League where he led Tottenham Hostpur and Chelsea before.

A new USMNT manager will be named. It could be someone as famous as Pep Guardiola. It may be someone known mostly to hardcore soccer fans.

That manager will call in Christian Pulisic. He will still be there, and he'll be there for the next manager, too.

The national team belongs to everyone, but every nation has its eras. Pulisic's started early, when he was the young hotshot on a team that missed the 2018 World Cup. He has passed from the great hope to the hero to ... whatever he is now. But he is part of the U.S. national team's present, and he's part of its future.

He reminded fans of that Friday, Nov. 14 with a Man of the Match showing in a 6-0 romp over Haiti.

This was not a friendly. The Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal series started Friday and will be decided Tuesday, Nov. 17. Except it was all but decided in the second half at Nu Stadium, with Pulisic helping to set up Julian Hall's goal to make it 2-0 in the 52nd minute, then scored two goals of his own − one from the penalty spot in the 62nd and another in the 63rd as soon as play resumed.

"Right after the goal I think it opened up a little bit. I got a ball with space, and kind of looked around and didn't see many good options and felt I could curl it in to the near post. That was it. I was feeling good, so yeah," he said.

Pulisic, Weston McKennie, Folarin Balogun and a few other vets missed out on the September-October window in which the U.S. played four friendly matches. Pochettino had the regulars stay with their clubs while obviously pressing the restart button and calling in talented teenagers.

"Thank you to Christian, thank you to Weston," Pochettino said. "They didn't participate in the last camp because we had half the squad made up of young kids. The way they were from the beginning was amazing. I think we can only say thank you."

Pulisic and Pochettino never seemed to have the closest relationship, with the player's decision not to play in the 2025 Gold Cup baffling the manager. When Pochettino was a player, any call from Argentina was sacred. Missing a continental championship was anathema.

Pulisic didn't see it that way, hoping to come in for pre-tournament friendly matches before getting a rest during the tournament proper

"I think we had some good moments and he brought a lot of excitement to the team," Pulisic said when asked what Pochettino's legacy would be with the U.S. "I think he'll leave that behind."

The AC Milan man is rarely verbose, but it was a succinct answer in a moment when he could've heaped praise on the outgoing coach.

But, no matter. Pochettino is gone, and Pulisic won't be headed to Manchester United to join him. He will, however, still be with the U.S. national team.

There already was talk after the September-October window that featured a bevy of top rising stars that the future may be now, that players like Cavan Sullivan and Hall were ready to be the focal points of the national team.

After all, Pulisic didn't hit the level he hoped to in the 2026 World Cup after the knock he suffered in the opener against Paraguay.

This, then, was a gentle reminder. No one was trying to put the 28-year-old out to pasture, but he still has plenty to say about the future of the national team − no matter who is in the technical area.

That is, though, the ideal. Now as it has been for a decade, the U.S. is better when Pulisic is contributing. A meld of Pulisic and Sullivan, allowing both to play to their strengths, would set the Stars and Stripes up perfectly.

Pulisic says he's ready to lend his leadership and example, if it's necessary.

"It's cool to see these guys, watch these kids in training. There's some really good players. For me, it's just exciting and I hope I can do everything I can to support them in any way I can," Pulisic said. "They don't need me, though. They're doing amazing."

Pulisic came into the window with three goals in his last five matches for AC Milan, and his future at the Serie A club secured with a long contract extension. He is feeling good wearing the Rossoneri and feeling good in the Stars and Stripes.

International teams always have ups and downs, but Pulisic also has a long future in the USMNT, especially if he continues to put in performances like he did Friday.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Christian Pulisic sends message with double vs. Haiti in USMNT return

Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay reacts during an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders in Las Vegas, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. Getty Images

#2640. 10 Takeaways: Avalanche Get Contributions From Up and Down the Lineup in Montreal

Everything about the way the Avalanche have played since losing Cale Makar and Nathan MacKinnon inspires confidence that this team can weather the storm. It's obviously still early, and things could change, but the initial returns have been extremely encouraging.

It's not just the 4-1 win over the Montreal Canadiens. It's how Colorado responded immediately after losing its two stars late in the second period against the Ottawa Senators two nights earlier. That night, the Avs erased a 2-0 deficit to take a 3-2 lead before eventually falling 4-3 in overtime. They found a way to earn a point in a game they probably had no business being in after those injuries.

To see them carry that over into Saturday night against another strong opponent is an encouraging sign. Colorado got production from every line, the power play came through, the penalty kill did its job, and Mackenzie Blackwood was locked in between the pipes once again.

The Avalanche finished their three-game road trip 2-0-1 and now have a few days back in Denver before heading to Utah for one more road game Wednesday.

Read NextPostgame Reaction: Avalanche Showed in Montreal That They Can Win Without Their Superstars

1. The first goal was huge. It had been eight road games since Colorado last scored first. Not only did the Avs finally break that streak, but they did it early in the first period to set the tone. They followed it up with another goal before the intermission.

It's nice to see Fedor Svechkov be the one to get the Avalanche on the board. It was just his third goal of the season and his first since Oct. 23. These are the games when you want to see your depth players set the tone, especially a fourth-line center stepping up in the first game without MacKinnon.

2. Brock Nelson followed Svechkov's goal by making it 2-0. It was Nelson's second goal in three games on the road trip after he had scored just once in his previous 11 games. Once again, it was a center stepping up in the absence of the team's superstar center.

3. I was curious to see who Bednar would put on the top line with MacKinnon unavailable. My initial thought was Nazem Kadri, given that he'd played that role with the Avs before and has chemistry with Artturi Lehkonen. But the more I thought about it, the more sense it made to put Nelson in that spot.

Kadri has been producing at a much more consistent rate than Nelson this season. There's no reason to disrupt that. Let Kadri continue doing his thing on the second or third line, surrounded by a supporting cast of wingers, and on the power play. It's been working for him. Nelson, meanwhile, hasn't produced at the same rate he did last season. Giving him an elevated role alongside Martin Necas and Lehkonen could help get him going.

4. Kadri wearing the 'A' was a nice touch. I know there are plenty of critics analyzing his play this season given his age, but I think he's been a great fit. He brings a spark and physical edge to the lineup that the Avs desperately missed after he left in 2022. It's still somewhat of a shock to see him back with the team. Seeing him serve as a leader and wear a letter is great, too. Much deserved.

5. Is there anything Lehkonen touches this season that doesn't turn to gold? In his first game on the top power-play unit, he came through with a big goal. What a guy.

6. Everything about that power-play goal was on brand for the players involved. Lehkonen was parked in the slot and got the initial shot on goal. Kadri crashed the crease looking to capitalize on the rebound before Lehkonen buried his second chance. Those are two guys who play scrappy hockey and fight for dirty goals. That's exactly what this was, and I mean that as a compliment.

7. What a game from Blackwood, who picked up his 11th win of the season. He's now 9-1-1 with a .917 save percentage and a shutout since that rough loss to Toronto at Ball Arena five weeks ago. He's been outstanding over that stretch, and the Avs will need him to keep it going with two of their biggest stars out of the lineup.

8. Congratulations to Alex Gagne on making his NHL debut. He held his own, playing 11:48 and finishing with three hits and three blocked shots. The Avs have high hopes for him, and I'll be curious to see what he does with this opportunity, even if it only lasts five or six games.

9. It's also nice to see Gavin Brindley back with the big club. He's a rhythm player who needs regular reps to get going. He didn't do much offensively in the 12 minutes he played against Montreal, but he's likely going to stick with the team for a month. It'll be interesting to see what he can do with a more extended opportunity.

10. Another player who stands to benefit from an extended opportunity? Sam Malinski.

Malinski has been playing better lately, dating back to when he started skating alongside Devon Toews. But with Makar out, he'll be relied upon far more than he was even a week ago. Against the Canadiens, he played a team-high 24:19. The only time he's logged more ice time was in Game 82 of the 2024-25 season, when several veterans sat out to prepare for the playoffs.

#2639. Sixers, Brown have a ‘humbling' night in loss to Celtics

Sixers, Brown have a 'humbling' night in loss to Celtics originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Whatever Jaylen Brown and the Sixers dreamed up for their first matchup against the Celtics soon flew out the window on Tuesday night.

Brown was whistled for two early fouls, the Sixers fell behind and their early-season flaws were on full display in a 123-101 loss at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

"We've just got to get better," Brown said. "Tonight was humbling. We got outplayed, out-executed. So we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the next one."

Over 26 minutes, Brown had 13 points on 4-for-9 shooting and five rebounds against the team that traded him away this summer.

As for the endless dissection of his relationship with former co-star Jayson Tatum, Brown didn't have much to add Tuesday. There was no public reconciliation, no obvious on-court animosity and generally nothing to satisfy fans hoping for some kind of fireworks on that front.

"I'm just focused on doing what's best for my team," Brown said. "Everything else … to be honest, I wasn't paying attention. But credit to Jayson; he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics. They executed, they shot the hell out of the ball and they were the better team tonight."

Tatum scored 21 points, two of which came on a third-quarter slam over LeBron James. Paul George continued his fantastic start as a Celtic by dropping 36 points and draining six three-pointers.

The Celtics dominated from beyond the arc, shooting 22 for 49 (44.9 percent). The Sixers went just 11 for 37 (29.7 percent) on another night of underwhelming offense. The team sits 22nd in the NBA in offensive rating, 24th in three-point makes per game and 21st in three-point percentage.

"I think that we've got some guys that are obviously shooting much lower percentages than their last season or their career average — almost a handful of guys," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "And I don't think it's because they're shooting fallaway, totally contested ones. I think they're shots we want them to take. So I think they'll continue to take 'em and I'm pretty sure those will even out into their career averages."

Joel Embiid is at 37 percent from the floor and 4 for 33 from three-point range (12.1 percent).

The Sixers' seven-time All-Star center got through an injury scare when he rolled his ankle late in the second quarter and hit a three early in the third. It was his first long-range make since the Sixers' home opener back on Oct. 22.

"It's a work in progress," Embiid said. "I think the biggest thing is just not thinking. I'm probably overthinking it. The rhythm of the game is different. I'm so used to having to create for myself, so it's a little bit different.

"But I think I'm slowly getting better. You could see as soon as I made a three, the next shot in the short corner … I didn't even think about it. I just shot it and let it fly, and I made it. … I think it's just about taking what's in front of you. Make or miss, keep working on your game. It's going to get there at some point."

Even with the Sixers second in the Eastern Conference standings at 9-3, Embiid believes the team's defense has "slacked off a little bit" in recent games.

"I don't really look at the record," he said. "I just look at the process of, 'Are we getting better every day?' We can always do a better job at all phases of the game."

"They're one of the top teams in the league and they've been together for a while," Brown said. "We've got a lot to work on over here, so we've got to get to work."

The Sixers will face the Raptors on Thursday night in Philadelphia.

They'll have to wait until Jan. 21 in Boston to see the Celtics again.

"I was looking forward to this," Brown said. "I was looking forward to playing well, but s— happens. Just get ready for the next one."

#2638. Cowboys vs 49ers: 2 players to buy, 2 to sell against San Francisco

The Dallas Cowboys are coming off a narrow win over the Indianapolis Colts, and now the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers are coming to town, bringing one of the league's most complete rosters and a defense that has consistently given Dallas problems in their recent matchups.

There are some opportunities for the Cowboys, particularly with CeeDee Lamb playing at a high level, but there are also some difficult matchups that could expose weaknesses on Dallas' roster. Here are two players to buy and two to sell ahead of Sunday's game.

I mean, who else would this list start with? Lamb has been the best player for the Cowboys all season, and there's no reason to think that Dallas will stop feeding him the ball. Lamb is coming off a monster performance against Indianapolis, hauling in 10 catches for 195 yards and a touchdown on 16 targets. It was his second-highest receiving total in a game during his career.

Through nine games, Lamb has 70 receptions for 904 yards and seven touchdowns. He's already surpassed the 900-yard mark, and his 108 targets lead the Cowboys by a wide margin. The matchup against San Francisco is difficult, but Lamb is the kind of receiver who can change a game regardless of the opponent. With George Pickens possibly missing another week and Dallas dealing with inconsistencies elsewhere the offense, Dak Prescott should continue looking Lamb's way early and often.

The 49ers will undoubtedly have a plan for him, but Lamb's recent production makes him difficult to leave out of the buyers market. He's been the Cowboys' most reliable playmaker overall, and Dallas needs to find ways to get him involved.

At some point, the Cowboys have to figure out how to beat San Francisco, and Dak Prescott has to be a big part of that solution. Unfortunately, his history against the 49ers doesn't inspire much confidence. Prescott is 2-4 against San Francisco in his career, including an 0-2 record in the playoffs. In those two postseason games, he has thrown for 460 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. His most recent regular-season meetings haven't been much better. He threw three interceptions in the 2023 blowout loss and two more in the 2024 matchup.

Across his four regular-season games against San Francisco, Prescott has completed 65.5% of his passes for 875 yards, eight touchdowns and five interceptions. That's not necessarily disastrous production, but the turnovers have been costly, particularly against a team that knows how to capitalize on mistakes.

The 49ers have won four straight meetings against Dallas, and Prescott will have to overcome both that team history and his own struggles against this opponent. San Francisco's defense is disciplined, physical and capable of making quarterbacks pay for forcing throws.

With Fred Warner leading the unit, Prescott will have to be sharp with his reads and decision-making, especially against the blitz, where he has looked terrible this year. Dallas needs a big performance from its quarterback to pull off the upset. Given the history, though, this is a matchup where I'm selling Prescott until he proves otherwise.

With Jake Ferguson ruled out due to a knee injury, Brevyn Spann-Ford has an opportunity to take on an even bigger role in the Cowboys' offense. It might not be the most obvious matchup to exploit, but he could be a sneaky contributor against San Francisco.

Spann-Ford has caught 15 passes for 130 yards this season, and his role has been growing. Against Indianapolis, he played 55 offensive snaps compared to Ferguson's 27, catching two of three targets for 20 yards. That workload suggests the Cowboys are already comfortable giving him significant playing time.

The 49ers have plenty of defensive talent to account for, and their attention will naturally gravitate toward Lamb and the Cowboys' other primary playmakers. That could leave opportunities for Spann-Ford underneath or in the middle of the field, particularly if Dallas uses him to help with protection before releasing him into a route.

This isn't a prediction that Spann-Ford is suddenly going to become the focal point of the passing game. Rather, it's a bet that his increased playing time and the attention paid to Dallas' other weapons could create a few favorable opportunities. With Ferguson unavailable, the Cowboys need someone else to contribute from the tight end position. Spann-Ford is in a good position to do that.

The Cowboys have indicated that Jaishawn Barham could see an increased workload as injuries continue to pile up on the defensive side of the ball. That's understandable from a personnel standpoint, but it also creates a potential problem against an offense as versatile as San Francisco's.

Barham had some encouraging moments early in the season, but his limitations have become more apparent as the competition has increased. His playing time has also been limited recently, which makes the prospect of a larger role against the 49ers particularly concerning.

San Francisco is exactly the type of opponent that can put a young linebacker in difficult situations. Kyle Shanahan's offense uses motion, misdirection and mismatches to create space, and open up running lanes.

If Dallas gives him more responsibility, San Francisco will have plenty of opportunities to test him. The Cowboys need all the help they can get defensively, but this is a tough week to ask an inconsistent young player to take on a bigger role.
